name: Serudung Murut
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: OLAC: resources in and about the Serudung Murut language [srk] (Internet Archive copy 2025-12-04).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Catalog only: lists Glottolog, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List entries; no SIL archive holdings for srk (so Lee 1998 and Rushing's materials are not publicly archived).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record and reference list for seru1246 (3 refs: Townsend 2017; Lobel 2016; Spitzack 1984).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Townsend, Joel. 2017. Reduplication in Serudung Murut. MA thesis (Linguistics), Leiden University. 95 pp. hdl:1887/52180 (Open Access).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 2.3 'Phonology and orthography' (pp. 11-16: vowel/consonant inventories, syllable structure, morphophonological processes) contains no statement on stress or accent; 'stress', 'accent', 'prosod-' occur nowhere in the thesis.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. Sec. 11.4.8 'The position of Murut Serudung', pp. 399-401.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Serudung: pp. 399-401 treat subgrouping only (pronoun table 11.24, *R reflexes, mu- reciprocal; Serudung groups with Paitanic, not Murutic).

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Southwest Sabah revisited. Oceanic Linguistics 52(1): 36-68.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Subgrouping article covering Murut Serudung with Lobel's own field transcriptions; low chance of an explicit stress remark but the transcriptions may carry accent marks.

sources.citation: Spitzack, John A. 1984. The Murutic language family. In Julie K. King & John Wayne King (eds.), Languages of Sabah: a survey report (Pacific Linguistics C-78), 155-223. Canberra: ANU. Sec. 3.12/4.12 'Serudung Murut language' (pp. 187, 210-211).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: survey data only (location, 350-450 speakers, lexicostatistics, intelligibility testing); the whole PL-C78 volume has no occurrence of 'stress'/'accent'/'penultimate'.

sources.citation: Rushing, Jack (SIL Malaysia). n.d. [c. 1991-2016]. Unpublished Serudung Murut materials: lexicon (c. 3000 items), 85 transcribed texts, rough grammatical sketch and orthography (cited by Townsend 2017:10-11).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only grammar sketch of the language by a long-term fieldworker; a phonology/orthography statement there is the most likely place for a stress rule.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2016. North Borneo Sourcebook: vocabularies and functors (PALI Language Texts: Southeast Asia). Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. Introduction pp. 1-7; 'Language Information' pp. 17-66; wordlists pp. 67-272 (Murut Serudung is one of the 46 languages).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked
sources.note: Only published source of Serudung Murut data (250-item wordlist); the Introduction/Language Information chapters may state transcription conventions for stress or give a per-language phonological note, and Lobel's transcriptions elsewhere mark accent.

sources.citation: Lee, Byung Hoon. 1998. Learn to speak Serudung Murut: a series of twenty-five language lessons. Unpublished manuscript, Summer Institute of Linguistics (Malaysia Branch).

sources.note: Pedagogical lessons often open with a pronunciation guide stating where stress falls; Townsend says copies may be held in SIL libraries/archives.
